name: Condición de Refugiado (CORE)

qualifying_event.description: A person with a well-founded fear of persecution, physically present in Uruguay, may apply for refugee status through the Comisión de Refugiados (CORE), reachable at the border/airport, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, SEDHU, the Migrant Reference Center in Montevideo, or any National Migration Directorate (DNM) office elsewhere in the country.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Completed personalized application form; identity document (or police report if unavailable); explanation of reasons for leaving the country of origin.

requirements.blocker_text: Applicant must be physically present in Uruguay to file (verbally or in writing). A refugee applicant certificate is issued on filing; a Migrant Certificate and ID card follow within 5-90 days (same-day for children under 9), then a personal interview, then a final resolution.

evidence_required.document: Personalized application form (not a generic template)
Identity document, or police report if unavailable

outcome.duration_length: indefinite upon recognition -- grants permanent residence directly

sources.title: ACNUR/UNHCR Uruguay -- Proceso de Solicitud: application locations, document requirements, 5-90 day ID processing, formal work rights during processing, permanent residence on recognition, 10-business-day judicial appeal

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Uruguay's initial build. Notably generous system, confirmed at tier-2 (UNHCR) with corroborating tier-1 context (gub.uy/ministerio-interior confirms CORE as the administering body and references a related 'Programa de Residencias por Arraigo' for asylum applicants who entered regularly, and ACNUR itself has publicly commended Uruguay as a 'model country' for refugee protection): applicants may work FORMALLY once they receive their provisional ID card -- well before a final decision -- and recognition grants PERMANENT residence directly, not a renewable temporary status as in most other countries built in this dataset. Denied applicants have 10 business days to seek judicial review via a lawyer, or may pursue other migratory regularisation instead. citizenship_after_months (36) assumes the 3-year 'family constituted' naturalisation track would often apply to a settled refugee, though this specific linkage was not independently confirmed by the source. gub.uy's own CORE page returned only an index-level description in this pass (limited detail beyond confirming the agency and the Arraigo program's existence) -- the operational detail here comes from UNHCR's process page instead.
